results.title: Stolen password, no second factor
results.attack: Attacker knows an enrolled user's password and guesses the one-time code.
results.control: Keycloak browser flow requires password AND OTP; the app also requires amr to contain a second factor.
results.evidence: wrong code answered with HTTP 200 "Invalid authenticator code."; no app session issued

results.title: Online brute force of the one-time code
results.attack: Attacker with the password submits many one-time codes.
results.control: Keycloak brute-force detection: temporary lockout after 5 failures (60 s, growing to 15 min).
results.evidence: account locked after 2 rapid failures (disabled=true, quick-login detection); correct credentials refused while locked; lockout cleared afterwards

results.title: Attacker enrols their own authenticator on a new account
results.attack: Attacker obtains a new user's initial password before the user's first sign-in and completes TOTP enrolment.
results.control: None in the prototype: first sign-in trusts whoever holds the initial password (trust-on-first-use).
results.evidence: attacker's authenticator was registered on the account. Mitigation: deliver initial passwords out of band as temporary, or use enrolment links

results.title: Tampered OAuth state on the callback
results.attack: Attacker sends the victim a callback URL with a forged state/code (login CSRF).
results.control: state, nonce and PKCE verifier are bound to an encrypted, short-lived transaction cookie.
results.evidence: callback answered 303 -> /login?error=token_exchange_failed&returnTo=%2Fdashboard

results.title: Cross-site request forgery
results.attack: A malicious site makes the admin's browser POST to logout, admin actions and the posture API.
results.control: Origin check on every state-changing endpoint, plus SameSite=Lax session cookie.
results.evidence: logout/admin/posture answered 403/403/403; target account unchanged

results.title: Open redirect after sign-in
results.attack: Phishing link with returnTo pointing to another site (incl. tab/newline and backslash tricks).
results.control: returnTo is resolved against the app origin; anything off-origin becomes /dashboard.
results.evidence: 6 hostile values tried, 0 escaped the app

results.title: Privilege escalation by an employee
results.attack: Employee opens admin pages, posts admin actions and requests the audit export.
results.control: Deny-by-default policy engine; admin.console / admin.manage require the tg-admin role from Keycloak.
results.evidence: admin page -> 307 /access-denied?resource=admin.console&returnTo=%2Fadmin%2Fusers; action -> access-denied; export -> 403

results.title: Automated browser (bot) inside a valid session
results.attack: Session is driven by automation (navigator.webdriver).
results.control: Device posture is re-reported and evaluated on every request; policy denies.
results.evidence: dashboard -> 307, decision DENY_SIGNAL (risk 100); access restored once the device was healthy

results.title: Forged posture report
results.attack: Client reports a different browser than it actually uses.
results.control: Device posture is re-reported and evaluated on every request; policy denies.
results.evidence: dashboard -> 307, decision DENY_SIGNAL (risk 70); access restored once the device was healthy

results.title: Non-compliant device
results.attack: Outdated browser on a page without a secure context.
results.control: Device posture is re-reported and evaluated on every request; policy denies.
results.evidence: dashboard -> 307, decision RISK_TOO_HIGH (risk 90); access restored once the device was healthy

results.title: Forged back-channel logout
results.attack: Attacker posts logout tokens (unsigned, and signed with their own key) to end a victim's session.
results.control: Logout tokens must be signed by the realm key (JWKS), with correct issuer, audience, event and age.
results.evidence: unsigned -> 400, attacker-signed -> 400; victim session active

results.title: Database leak exposes usable sessions or tokens
results.attack: Attacker reads the sessions table (e.g. backup leak) and tries to reuse what is stored.
results.control: Only SHA-256 hashes of session ids are stored; Keycloak tokens are AES-256-GCM encrypted.
results.evidence: 0 of 75 stored sessions contain a raw JWT or cookie value; presenting the stored hash as a cookie -> 307

results.title: Tampering with the audit trail
results.attack: An insider with application-level database access edits or deletes audit records.
results.control: Trigger makes trustguard.audit_events append-only (UPDATE and DELETE raise errors).
results.evidence: UPDATE and DELETE rejected: "audit_events is append-only". (A database owner could still drop the trigger.)

results.title: Spoofed client IP address
results.attack: Client sends a forged X-Forwarded-For header to choose the IP the app sees.
results.control: Only effective behind a reverse proxy that overwrites X-Forwarded-For (not part of the prototype).
results.evidence: app recorded the attacker-chosen IP 198.51.100.77; IP-based signals are only trustworthy behind a proxy

results.title: Admin action from an old sign-in
results.attack: Someone uses an admin's unattended browser 31 minutes after sign-in to suspend a user.
results.control: admin.manage policy: actions need a sign-in under 30 minutes old (step-up otherwise).
results.evidence: action redirected to step-up re-authentication; user not suspended

results.title: Abandoned session reused later
results.attack: A session left idle for 2 hours is picked up again.
results.control: 30-minute sliding idle timeout and 8-hour absolute lifetime, enforced server-side.
results.evidence: request -> 307; session expired (idle_timeout)

results.title: Session fixation
results.attack: Attacker plants a known session cookie in the victim's browser before the victim signs in.
results.control: A new random session id is issued at every sign-in; the planted value is never a valid session.
results.evidence: victim received a new session id; planted cookie -> 307

results.title: Authorization code replay
results.attack: Attacker captures the victim's callback URL (code + state) and replays it.
results.control: Code is bound to the victim's transaction cookie and PKCE verifier, and is single-use at Keycloak.
results.evidence: replay from attacker -> /login?error=transaction_missing; replay in victim's browser -> /login?error=transaction_missing

results.title: Tokens exposed to the browser (XSS impact)
results.attack: Script injected into a page tries to read access/refresh/ID tokens or the session cookie.
results.control: BFF pattern: tokens never leave the server; the session cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax.
results.evidence: 7 app responses during sign-in, 0 contained a JWT; session cookie HttpOnly + SameSite=Lax: true

results.title: Stolen session cookie used from another device
results.attack: Attacker copies the victim's session cookie (malware, shared PC) into their own browser.
results.control: Sessions are bound to the device cookie of the browser that verified posture; mismatch revokes the session.
results.evidence: thief -> 307 /login?error=device_mismatch; session revoked (device_mismatch), victim must sign in again

results.title: Revoked user signs straight back in via SSO
results.attack: After an admin ends their session, the user relies on Keycloak's SSO cookie to get back in silently.
results.control: Ending a session also ends the Keycloak SSO session via the least-privilege service account.
results.evidence: after revocation the sign-in shows the password form again (no silent SSO)

results.title: Suspended employee keeps working
results.attack: A suspended user (e.g. leaving the company) tries to continue or sign in again.
results.control: Suspension disables the Keycloak account first, then ends every session.
results.evidence: sign-in refused by Keycloak: "Account is disabled, contact your administrator." (account reactivated afterwards)
